How to use Waffle Player

Waffle Player home / 日本語

Waffle Player plays and compares multiple videos and images side by side in a tiled grid, all in sync. Compare different edits, export settings, or camera angles at a glance. The red boxes and numbers in the images match the numbers in the text.

1. Load videos

  • Drag and drop videos or images onto the window. You can drop as many as you like at once
  • Drop a folder to load the videos and images in its subfolders too
  • When nothing is loaded, double-click the box in the middle (1) to choose files
  • You can also open MP4, MOV, MKV, and WebM files with Waffle Player from File Explorer (if it is already running, they are added to that window)
  • When you load more than 9 files at once, you are asked to confirm (more files put more load on your PC)

Supported formats

TypeFormats
VideoMP4, MOV, MKV, WebM (H.264, H.265/HEVC, VP8, VP9, AV1)
ImagesPNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, AVIF

Editing codecs such as ProRes and DNxHD, AVI, MTS, WMV, FLV, MXF, and TIFF images are not supported. A video that can't be played shows "This video can't be played" in its frame. Playing H.265 requires a GPU with hardware H.265 decoding.

2. Play (control bar)

Use the control bar at the bottom of the window.

No.Button / displayWhat it does
1To startGo to marker A, or the start (Home)
2Play / PausePlay or pause every video together (Space)
3Seek barClick or drag to move the position. Hold Shift while dragging to snap to a fixed step counted from frame 0 (10 frames by default)
4Remaining / totalBased on the longest video
5CCCycle captions (C)
6ClearRemove all videos
7CameraGo to capture mode
8ClipboardCopy the current view
9PNGSave the current view as PNG
10GearSettings
  • Every video plays in sync with the longest one. Shorter videos hold on their last frame when they end
  • If your PC can't keep up (for example, with many videos at once) and a video can't be shown at its original frame rate, a warning appears at the top: "Playback is too heavy to show the original frame rate" (when it stays below 90% for 3 seconds; it disappears once playback recovers). Playing fewer videos or using a smaller window helps
  • Step one frame with ← / → or the mouse wheel, 1/3 second with Shift, and 1 second with Alt

Seek bar handles and markers

  • Hover over a handle on the seek bar (position, A, or B) to show a "marker" right above it, with the time in seconds and the frame number
  • You can also drag the marker to move the handle. The marker stays visible while you drag
  • Hold Shift while dragging to snap to a fixed step counted from frame 0 (with 10 frames: frame 0, 10, 20, ...). Set the step in frames or seconds with "Shift + drag step" in the gear menu
  • While you step frames with ← / → or the mouse wheel, and for about 2 seconds after, the position marker is shown

3. Loop a section (A / B markers)

  • Press [ to set marker A and ] to set marker B at the current position
  • The section between A and B loops. Drag the A and B handles to move them (hover over them to see the time and frame marker)

4. Show captions

Press C or the CC button (2) to cycle through:

ModeShows
CC (off)Nothing
CC₁ (detail)File name, resolution, frame rate, codec, duration, total frames, current time and frame number
CC₂ (name only)The file name, large in the middle
CC₃ (name and frame)The file name and the current frame number, in one small line in a corner
  • Frame numbers count from "Start frame" in the gear menu (0 by default; set it to 1, 1001, or whatever your studio uses)
  • Move captions to any corner by dragging them, with Ctrl + arrow keys, or with "Caption position" in the gear menu
  • Change their size with "Caption size" in the gear menu

5. Show one video large

Double-click a video to show just that one large. Double-click again, or press Esc, to return.

6. Right-click menu (audio, empty cells, and more)

ItemWhat it does
Single viewShow just that video large
Play this video's audio (1)Play only that video's sound. All videos start muted
Time shiftShift when that video starts playing (see "7. Time shift")
Open folder in ExplorerOpen the folder containing the file
Copy full path / Copy file nameCopy where the file is, or its name
Add dummy (2)Insert an empty cell after it
Remove this videoRemove that video
  • Reorder: drag a video onto the one you want to swap with
  • Empty cells: drag the checkered cells around too, to arrange the layout however you like. You can add as many as the number of videos loaded. Right-click an empty cell to remove it

7. Time shift (offset playback timing)

You can shift when each video starts playing. Use it to line up clips whose start points differ, or footage that moved earlier or later in the edit. Right-click a video and enter a value under "Time shift".

No.ItemWhat it does
1secThe shift in seconds. + starts later, − starts earlier
2framesThe shift in frames. Enter either one and the other updates automatically (snapped to that video's frames)
3RangeHow far you can shift: earlier, until the video's last frame reaches frame 0; later, up to the length of the longest loaded video
4Reset time shiftSet this video's shift back to 0
5Reset time shift on all cellsSet every video's shift back to 0
  • Not started yet (1): a video shifted later holds its first frame, dimmed, until it starts
  • Shifted videos (2, 3): a label such as "⇄ +48 f" above the cell shows the shift. Click it to open a time shift window over every video, with a slider as well as the input fields (the slider covers the full range, earlier and later, and a white tick marks 0, no shift; hold Shift while sliding to snap to a fixed step counted from 0)
  • Original frame 0 (4): while any video is shifted, a blue line on the seek bar marks frame 0 of the unshifted videos. If a video is shifted earlier, the seek bar starts before 0 (for example -0:01)
  • A video keeps its time shift when you reorder the grid or add or remove other videos
  • If removing a video makes "the longest video" shorter so that a shift is out of range, the message "The time shift limit changed, so it was adjusted automatically" appears and the shift is brought back into range
  • Time shifts go back to 0 when you close the app

8. Copy or save the view

Use the clipboard button to copy the current view, or the PNG button to save it as a PNG file.

  • Left-click: export at the displayed size
  • Right-click: choose "native size (100%)" or "displayed size"

9. Add notes in capture mode

Press the camera button to turn the current view into a still image you can write on. Use it to send revision notes or feedback as an image right away.

No.ToolWhat it does
1HandMove the view (double-click the striped area to reset it)
2SelectSelect notes to move or edit them
3–6Arrow, line, circle, rectangleDraw shapes
7TextWrite text
8PenDraw freehand
9PastePaste an image from the clipboard (Ctrl + V)
10ColorsChoose from 7 colors
11WidthLine width (font size for text)
12CCCycle the captions in the exported image (off → CC₁ detail → CC₂ name only → CC₃ name and frame)
13ZoomZoom with the mouse wheel; double-click to return to 100%
14UndoUndo (Ctrl + Z)
15TrimLimit the area to copy or save
16ClipboardCopy the annotated view (right-click to choose the size)
17PNGSave the annotated view as PNG (right-click to choose the size)
18✕ CloseReturn to the player
  • Right-click a note to bring it to front, send it to back, duplicate, or delete it. Delete also deletes it
  • Notes are not kept, so copy or save before you close

10. Settings (gear menu)

No.ItemWhat it sets
1Caption sizeSize of the caption text
2Caption positionThe corner for captions (↖ ↗ ↙ ↘). Same as Ctrl + arrow keys
3Start frameThe first frame number shown in captions and markers (0, 1, 1001, ... typed in)
4VolumeVolume of the video whose audio is playing
5Shift + drag stepThe step that Shift + drag on the seek bar snaps to. A number, in frames or seconds
6LanguageDisplay language (10 languages)
7How to useOpen this page in your browser
8AboutVersion, days left in the free trial, and licenses of the software used
9Keyboard shortcutsA list of key operations
